minutes.headline: Budget Task Force heard the Capital Planning Committee chair on how capital requests are prioritized without a funding plan; no votes.
minutes.summary: The task force spent most of the meeting questioning a capital planning committee member (a school committee representative) about how capital requests are ranked, why no fiscal forecast or funding plan accompanies them, and whether rolling stock should move into operating budgets or special-purpose stabilization funds and targeted overrides. Members then planned the next two meetings (expense reduction ideas, revenue ideas, talking points for a five-minute town meeting update) and discussed the 2015-2016 drop in miscellaneous non-recurring revenue, which the town accountant traced to bond proceeds. Public comment covered solar at the old dump, the Mad Max "crisis" framing, and the Marshall Park project. No votes were taken.

public_comment.topic: Opening public comment: Anna asked, none offered at the start.

Anna suggested a shared-revenue solar field at the old town dump (as Grafton has), noted a prior $25,000 ARPA request, and said Lunenburg is not in a 'Mad Max' crisis but has not decided how to care for infrastructure.

Anna, former Parks Commission chair, responded to last meeting's reaction to the Marshall Park cost, saying the project was planned with the previous town manager and that regular debt has been falling.
Discussion with Anna of solar at the dump: state contracts, brownfield money, compost sales from yard waste; she offered to help with slides.

budget_items.what_was_said: Out-year capital requests from last year exist, but this year's requests are not all in; presentations start next week and run into early November.
Historically the amount funded is typically less than half of what was requested, and over five years the gap is tens of millions.
Free cash and other sources suggest no substantial increase in available capital next year.

budget_items.topic: Special purpose stabilization fund for large vehicles
budget_items.what_was_said: A stabilization fund for fire trucks, ambulances and large vehicles is funded each year and feeds the capital plan.
A new loader was proposed while keeping the old one as backup; committee members split over the cost.
figures_as_heard: a quarter of a million dollar piece of equipment

budget_items.what_was_said: A tractor was bought rather than contracting the work; the cost-benefit analysis was described as unconvincing.

budget_items.topic: Paying for rolling stock under Prop 2.5
budget_items.what_was_said: Carter explained cash, debt and exclusions differ in effect on the operating budget under the levy limit, using a cruiser example.
Reportedly Ashby funds its capital plan each year through a one-year exclusion that goes to ballot annually.

budget_items.topic: Targeted capital override tied to stabilization fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Carter described Grafton's targeted override for roads and capital, which must be raised in the first year and can be accumulated.
Mailing the warrant costs a few thousand dollars a year and a postcard notice could save part of that and give two more weeks.
Discussion of unused levy capacity; a past left-behind amount was tied to an abatement year, and FY24 close-out is pending.
A drop around 2015-2016 in a local revenue category was examined, with guesses of grants or MSBA reimbursement.
The accountant's MUNIS report showed school construction bond proceeds posted to miscellaneous non-recurring revenue in 2015 and 2016, which may explain the cliff.

budget_items.topic: Solar at old dump and ARPA request
budget_items.what_was_said: A prior ARPA request for solar at the old dump was mentioned; no formal request was ever presented.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force took no votes and spent most of the meeting questioning a Capital Planning Committee member on how capital requests are ranked and why no funding plan accompanies them.
Members discussed moving rolling stock into operating budgets, special-purpose stabilization funds, or targeted overrides, and heard how cash, debt and exclusions differ under the levy limit.
The town accountant traced the 2015-2016 drop in miscellaneous non-recurring revenue to bond proceeds, and will upload the MUNIS report to the shared drive.
The task force set its next meeting for October 7 and planned a roughly five-minute town meeting update given by two members.
In public comment, a resident proposed a shared-revenue solar field at the old dump, and a member agreed to email about presenting a solar proposal.

why_it_matters: Capital requests for vehicles, equipment and buildings are ranked each year without a funding plan, so how they are paid for (cash, debt, a stabilization fund or a targeted override) decides whether a resident sees them as a ballot question or inside the operating budget.
A revenue drop that is bond proceeds, not lost recurring income, changes which revenue gaps the task force's town meeting talking points can fairly describe.
